title: perf(route): status line reads a json precomputed by route.drive, never a fresh node per update
description:
## .what

make the route status line cheap: it should read a precomputed json, never start a fresh `node` per update. at minimum, debounce its real work to once per minute.

## .why

- the status line installed by `init.claude.status-line` runs `node -e "import('rhachet-roles-bhrain/cli/route').then(m => m.routeStatusLine())"` — a fresh node process, plus a module import, on every status update, in every claude session
- claude code docs (statusline, "When the status line updates"): the status line re-runs on session events, and on a `refreshInterval` timer if one is set; if a new update triggers while a slow status command runs, the in-flight run is cancelled. so a slow command is started often, and often thrown away
- measured on a dev box with ~10 live claude sessions: `node -e import('rhachet-roles-bhrain/cli/route')...routeStatusLine()` shows up repeatedly among the newborn processes in a churn sample, beside a box-wide rate of 600-1300 forks/sec

## .proposed shape — two options, either beats today

1. **precompute (preferred):** `route.drive` (and every route operation that changes the shown state — `route.stone.set`, `route.bind.set`, ...) writes the status-line text to a small json beside the bound route. the status line command becomes a plain file read (`cat` / `jq`, or a shell builtin), with no node start at all
2. **debounce (floor):** if precompute is not yet in place, cache the rendered line with a timestamp and recompute at most once per minute; every other update serves the cached line

## .acceptance

- a status-line update starts no `node` process when the route state has not changed
- the shown line still reflects a stone change on the next update after it
- measured before/after: node births per minute per session from the status line

## .sources

- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline
